structured_plan.G: Retain the supplied baseline until candidates pass correctness checks. Compare validated programs on the official mixed-width workload using compatible measurements; do not assume gains combine. Integrate the best confirmed candidate and independently confirm the final G before replacing the baseline.
structured_plan.analysis: Choose N=3 for distinct paths: validate every byte with SIMD, accelerate ASCII blocks while retaining scalar validation for non-ASCII, and improve the scalar parser without SIMD. This covers the main plausible costs without duplicating the same strategy. The supplied baseline is correct and measured at about 49.63 µs over three trials; this is a reference, not an independent confirmation. Performance is specified for n=65536 mixed-width text; ASCII and malformed inputs remain correctness requirements. No candidate measurements are available yet.

children.objective: Explore whole-buffer SIMD UTF-8 validation: classify byte roles and detect invalid continuation structure and restricted lead/second-byte combinations across blocks. Handle cross-block sequences and every tail length without out-of-range loads. Preserve the run signature, thread budget, input immutability, complete output write, and correctness for all byte sequences. Compile and measure only valid candidates on the official workload.
children.subject: SIMD validation of all byte classes

children.objective: Explore word- or vector-width detection and skipping of all-ASCII blocks, falling back to the supplied scalar validator at non-ASCII bytes and safely resuming block scanning afterward. Do not read past n or assume padding. Preserve all correctness and interface constraints; assess gains on the mixed-width workload, not only ASCII.
children.subject: ASCII block elision with scalar fallback

children.objective: Explore a distinct non-SIMD scalar approach, such as a compact byte-class DFA or branch-light code-point parser, to reduce per-byte branches and overhead on mixed-width data. Cover malformed continuations, overlong forms, surrogates, out-of-range values, and truncation at every boundary. Preserve all interface and memory constraints; retain only measured, correct improvements.
children.subject: Branch-light scalar UTF-8 parser
